newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-WEEKEND FIXTURES IN THE SPANISH FIRST DIVISION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEEKEND FIXTURES IN THE SPANISH FIRST DIVISION.

text.p: Matches to be played this weekend in the Spanish first division:
(numbers in brackets indicate league standings)
Saturday:
Barcelona (1) v Atletico Madrid (6) kick-off 1930 gmt
Barcelona are without half a dozen key players, amongst them striker Ronaldo, to face a rapidly improving Atletico outfit who hope to have set-piece man Milinko Pantic fit for action.
Athletic Bilbao (12) v Valencia (9) 1600
Athletic golden boy Julen Guerrero hopes to continue his four-game goal run against a Valencia side that has lost Valery Karpin and Goran Vlaovic to international duty.
Extremadura (21) v Sevilla (17) 1600
Greek international Varsilis Tsartas will miss what promises to be a good opportunity for the Sevilla forwards to prove themselves before the arrival of Brazilian striker Bebeto.
Real Madrid (2) v Logrones (18) 1600
Real will look to Raul Gonzalez for firepower in the absence of Clarence Seedorf, Predrag Mijatovic and Davor Suker against a team that has never won in the Bernabeu stadium
Celta Vigo (14) v Compostela (19) 1600
Compostela hope to end a run of abysmal bad luck by winning for the third consecutive season at Galician rivals Celta, who also badly need the points.
Hercules (22) v Zaragoza (20) 1600
The Spanish saying that teams with new managers always win, will certainly be broken in what already looks like a relegation struggle between teams that each fired managers midweek.
Real Betis (5) v Real Sociedad (7) 1600
Real Sociedad have run out of steam after a good start while Betis tend to lose at home what they win away. Each side has lost three key foreigners to World Cup qualifiers.
Rayo Vallecano (11) v Racing Santander (8) 1600
Rayo's Brazilian striker Guilherme and Racing's Uruguayan goalscorer Fernando Correa are the danger men in a clash between two teams that have done better than expected.
Oviedo (16) v Espanyol (13) 1600
World Cup matches mean Oviedo will be without four players, and Espanyol three.
Deportivo Coruna (3) v Tenerife (10) 1830
With five players away, among them influential goalkeeper Jacques Songo'o, Deportivo are the team most affected by World Cup commitments, while Tenerife are also without three players.
Monday:
Valladolid (4) v Sporting Gijon (15) 2030
Unfancied Valladolid hope to keep their surprise start going with a win at Sporting Gijon, who have become Spain's Monday team because of a contract with a television company.
